title.en: The Cession of Thessaly and Arta

summary.en: Following the Congress of Berlin, the Ottoman Empire ceded Thessaly and the district of Arta to Greece without a war. Greece had mobilised but had not fought. The settlement left Elassona on the Ottoman side of the new line, where it stayed until 1912.

body_html.en:
Greece had stayed out of the Russo-Turkish War of 1877 and 1878 and had been rewarded at Berlin with a recommendation, not a grant, that the Porte should rectify the frontier in Greece's favour. Three years of negotiation and a Greek mobilisation in 1880 followed.

The convention signed at Constantinople in 1881 gave Greece the plain of Thessaly and the district of Arta, about a quarter more territory and three hundred thousand people. It fell short of the line Berlin had suggested: Elassona, Preveza and the rest of Epirus stayed Ottoman for another generation.

sources.title: Modern Greece: A History since 1821
sources.author: John S. Koliopoulos and Thanos M. Veremis
